A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MMFakeBench and MMD-Agent. The complete main texts and appendices, including tables, figures, and equations, support comparison despite substantial additions and reorganization in v3.

before.justification: V2 reports original evaluations of detection methods and LVLMs, MMD-Agent ablations, source-specific performance, and error analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains those empirical results and adds human evaluation, knowledge-source ablations, cross-dataset comparisons, fine-tuning experiments, efficiency measurements, and benchmark analyses.

M1.justification: MMD-Agent retains its three-stage checks, intermediate reasoning/actions, and Wikipedia retrieval. V3's separate Thought/Observation terminology describes components already illustrated in v2; it does not establish a new model, objective, or inference procedure.

E1.justification: V3 adds standalone evaluations on NewsCLIPpings and Fakeddit and evaluates retention on DGM4 after adaptation to MMFakeBench (Tables 7 and 9). These datasets previously served as construction sources or detector background, rather than separately evaluated populations. MMFakeBench's own 11,000-pair coverage remains unchanged.

E2.justification: Human evaluation becomes an additional comparator in Tables 2 and 6. The original six-detector and 15-LVLM comparisons are retained. FKA-Owl matches the earlier FakeNewsGPT4 work through its authors, title, and citation context; it is not an additional detector.

E3.justification: V3 introduces an 80-participant study with 50 randomly selected questions per questionnaire from the 1,000-item validation bank, fine-tuning budgets of 10/100/1,000 examples, and efficiency and diversity evaluations. Section 3.1.1 also changes the reported supporting-image selection rule from exceeding a CLIP threshold to choosing the highest-scoring images, without establishing dataset regeneration. Original splits and classification metrics remain.

E4.justification: V3 adds removal/substitution of external knowledge, adaptation and forgetting analyses, efficiency measurements, relevancy maps, and dataset-diversity diagnostics. Four-model failure cases replace v2's two-model example comparisons. The original hierarchical ablations and misinformation-type analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V3's deterministic decoding disclosure and descriptive entropy measurements do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Previously reported model scores in Tables 2–6 are retained. Added results include human F1 scores of 35.9 for multiclass and 54.9 for binary classification. LLaVA-1.6-34B achieves 43.8 without Wikipedia and 48.5 with Google knowledge, versus the retained 49.9 with Wikipedia; inference takes 49.04 seconds with MMD-Agent versus 5.97 with standard prompting. Tables 7, 9, and 10 add cross-dataset, fine-tuning, and dataset-statistics results.

T1.justification: Equation (1) separates retrieved observations from reasoning traces, re-expressing knowledge retrieval already present in v2. No substantive mathematical assumptions, proofs, or theoretical guarantees are added. The new entropy calculations are descriptive benchmark measurements.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the first comprehensive mixed-source benchmark, covering three misinformation sources and 12 forgery types, evaluate six detectors and 15 LVLMs, and propose MMD-Agent to improve detection. Naming MMD-Agent in the abstract and emphasizing fine-grained evaluation do not materially change these contributions.

C2.justification: V3 adds interpretations of external-knowledge dependence, artificial versus natural rumor difficulty, inference-cost tradeoffs, and catastrophic forgetting after fine-tuning. New case analyses discuss overlooked physical anomalies and distraction by globally consistent semantics. The existing limitation concerning inadequate Wikipedia retrieval is relocated, rather than newly introduced.

D1.justification: V3 newly specifies eight 3090 GPUs, the GPT-4 model identifier, deterministic decoding, a 512-token generation limit, and ten volunteers selecting manipulated images. It also documents dataset licenses and states that detection code is released, generation code withheld, and data access restricted to verified researchers under an agreement. These expand v2's configuration and access documentation; they do not establish changed inference settings or withdrawal of previously available code.

R1.justification: V3 adds citations concerning image generation/editing, co-attention detection, and LVLM interpretability, including Cui et al., Wu et al., and Stan et al. Related-work discussion is modestly revised while the mixed-source novelty positioning remains. FakeNewsGPT4's update to the published FKA-Owl reference is matched as the same work.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the prose remain. Targeted revisions rewrite source definitions and the framework explanation, standardize reasoning terminology, subdivide the appendix, and move ethics/limitations into the main text. Conference headers, author ordering, and citation style also change.

P2.justification: The overview and framework diagrams are redesigned, and v2 Figure 2 is split and redrawn as v3 Figures 2–3. V2 Figures 6–7 are combined into v3 Figure 7. Expanded comparison tables, new Tables 7–10, replacement error-analysis displays, relevancy maps, diversity plots, and dataset-example galleries substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 lacked direct measurements of human difficulty, retrieval's contribution, and computational overhead. V3 supplies these alongside cross-dataset and adaptation evidence, substantially strengthening benchmark validation and exposing MMD-Agent's accuracy–latency tradeoff. Configuration and access documentation also improve assessability. Fine-tuning protocols remain underspecified and uncertainty reporting is absent, but the added evidence materially improves the paper.
